items.sentence_raw: The Lumière Brothers opened their Cinematographe, at 14 Boulevard des Capucines in Paris, to 100 paying customers over 100 years ago, on December 8, 1895.
items.explain: Q1: The question asks for the **location** of the first cinema. The passage says the Lumière Brothers opened their Cinematographe *'at 14 Boulevard des Capucines in Paris'*. This is the exact address, so the answer is **A**.

items.sentence_raw: Before the eyes of the stunned, thrilled audience, photographs came to life and moved across a flat screen.
So ordinary and routine has this become to us that it takes a determined leap of the imagination to grasp the impact of those first moving images.

But it is worth trying, for to understand the initial shock of those images is to understand the extraordinary power and magic of cinema, the unique, hypnotic quality that has made film the most dynamic, effective art form of the 20th century.
items.explain:
Q6: The question says it is **important** to understand the first audience's reaction. The passage says *'it is worth trying, for to understand the initial shock... is to understand the extraordinary power and magic of cinema'*. **'Worth trying'** means it is important, so the answer is **YES**.

Q13: The best title is **The power of the big screen**. The whole passage talks about cinema's magic, its impact on audiences, and how it changed the world. The first paragraph says understanding this shock is to understand the *'extraordinary power and magic of cinema'*, which is the main idea. So the answer is **D**.

items.sentence_raw: One of the Lumière Brothers' earliest films was a 30-second piece which showed a section of a railway platform flooded with sunshine.
A train appears and heads straight for the camera.
And that is all that happens.
Yet the Russian director Andrei Tarkovsky, one of the greatest of all film artists, described the film as a 'work of genius'.
"As the train approached," wrote Tarkovsky, "panic started in the theatre: people jumped and ran away.
items.explain: Q10: The writer uses the train film to show the **impact** of early films. The passage describes how the audience *'panicked'* and *'jumped and ran away'*, showing the powerful effect. ***Option A is a trap*** — the film was simple, but the purpose is to show the audience's strong reaction, not the film's simplicity. So the answer is **B**.

items.sentence_raw: Pictures were still, only reality moved; this must, therefore, be reality.
In their confusion, they feared that a real train was about to crush them."
Early cinema audiences often experienced the same confusion.
In time, the idea of film became familiar, the magic was accepted - but it never stopped being magic.
Film has never lost its unique power to embrace its audiences and transport them to a different world.
For Tarkovsky, the key to that magic was the way in which cinema created a dynamic image of the real flow of events.
A still picture could only imply the existence of time, while time in a novel passed at the whim of the reader.
But in cinema, the real, objective flow of time was captured.
items.explain: Q11: Tarkovsky believed cinema's attraction is that it **illustrates the passing of time**. The passage says *'in cinema, the real, objective flow of time was captured'*. This means cinema shows time moving in a real way, unlike a still picture. So the answer is **C**.

items.sentence_raw: One effect of this realism was to educate the world about itself.
For cinema makes the world smaller.
Long before people travelled to America or anywhere else, they knew what other places looked like; they knew how other people worked and lived.
items.explain: Q4: The question asks how cinema teaches us about **other cultures**. The passage says people *'knew what other places looked like; they knew how other people worked and lived'*. This shows cinema educated people about the world, so the answer is **E**.

items.sentence_raw: Overwhelmingly, the lives recorded - at least in film fiction - have been American.
From the earliest days of the industry, Hollywood has dominated the world film market.
American imagery - the cars, the cities, the cowboys - became the primary imagery of film.
Film carried American life and values around the globe.
And, thanks to film, future generations will know the 20th century more intimately than any other period.
We can only imagine what life was like in the 14th century or in classical Greece.
But the life of the modern world has been recorded on film in massive, encyclopaedic detail.
We shall be known better than any preceding generations.
The 'star' was another natural consequence of cinema.
items.explain: Q5: The question asks about the **attraction of actors**. The passage introduces the *'star'* as a *'natural consequence of cinema'* and explains how film personalities become *'super-real'*. This is the attraction of actors, so the answer is **G**.

items.sentence_raw: The cinema star was effectively born in 1910.
Film personalities have such an immediate presence that, inevitably, they become super-real.
Because we watch them so closely and because everybody in the world seems to know who they are, they appear more real to us than we do ourselves.
The star as magnified human self is one of cinema's most strange and enduring legacies.
Cinema has also given a new lease of life to the idea of the story.
When the Lumière Brothers and other pioneers began showing off this new invention, it was by no means obvious how it would be used.
All that mattered at first was the wonder of movement.
items.explain: Q9: The question says **storylines were important** in very early cinema. The passage says *'All that mattered at first was the wonder of movement'*. This directly contradicts the question — movement, not story, was important. So the answer is **NO**.

items.sentence_raw: Indeed, some said that, once this novelty had worn off, cinema would fade away.
items.explain: Q12: When cinema began, people thought its **future was uncertain**. The passage says some believed it *'would fade away'* and was *'no more than a passing gimmick'*. This shows they did not know if it would last. So the answer is **D**.

items.sentence_raw: Cinema might, for example, have become primarily a documentary form.
Or it might have developed like television - as a strange, noisy transfer of music, information and narrative.
But what happened was that it became, overwhelmingly, a medium for telling stories.
items.explain: Q2: The question asks how cinema came to **focus on stories**. The passage explains that cinema *'became, overwhelmingly, a medium for telling stories'*. This directly states the change, so the answer is **I**.

items.sentence_raw: Originally these were conceived as short stories - early producers doubted the ability of audiences to concentrate for more than the length of a reel.
Then, in 1912, an Italian 2-hour film was hugely successful, and Hollywood settled upon the novel-length narrative that remains the dominant cinematic convention of today.
And it has all happened so quickly.
items.explain: Q3: The question asks about the **speed** of cinema's change. The passage says *'And it has all happened so quickly'*. **'Quickly'** means with great speed, so the answer is **J**.

items.sentence_raw: Almost unbelievably, it is a mere 100 years since that train arrived and the audience screamed and fled, convinced by the dangerous reality of what they saw, and, perhaps, suddenly aware that the world could never be the same again - that, maybe, it could be better, brighter, more astonishing, more real than reality.

orphan_explain_map.7: Q7: The passage describes the train film as a *'work of genius'* by one director, but it never says it was **one of the greatest films ever made**. This is a personal opinion that the passage does not give. ***NOT GIVEN is not the same as FALSE***, so the answer is **NOT GIVEN**.
orphan_explain_map.8: Q8: The passage says Hollywood dominated and carried American life around the globe, but it never says this view is **biased**. The passage does not judge if this is fair or unfair. ***The passage gives facts, not an opinion on bias***, so the answer is **NOT GIVEN**.
